brief.summary: The website of a volunteer-run neighborhood monthly newspaper, holding the current issue, nearly four decades of digitized back issues and pages about the people and places it covers.
brief.user: Walt Hennessey, a 71-year-old retired machinist who has lived on Tannery Street since 1979. He reads the paper in print, but this is his first time using the new website, which the volunteers launched last month.
brief.moment: His neighbor told him the Gazette ran a story about the 1994 flood that damaged Tannery Street, with a photo of his old garage. He wants to find it to show his grandson, who's visiting this weekend. Along the way he's also trying to find this month's holiday events for the neighborhood. He keeps losing track of whether he's in the current issue or the archive and how to get back to where he was. He doesn't know the article title or the exact month, only that it was spring or summer 1994.
brief.data: 452 issues from March 1988 to November 2026, each with its issue number, month and 16–28 pages of articles. Regular sections: Neighborhood News, Letters, Council Watch, Schools, Obituaries, Events, Then & Now. About 9,800 articles from 1988–2009 digitized with OCR text (with errors like 'Tannerv St.'), and 4,100 born-digital articles since 2010. Tags for 14 neighborhood areas and 210 street names. Contributor pages for 186 volunteer writers and photographers. Matching 1994 articles: 'Millrace Overflows its Banks' (May 1994, p. 1), 'Tannery Street Digs Out' (June 1994, p. 3, 4 photos), and a July 1994 letter about flood relief. The November 2026 issue has 22 articles, including a Holiday Events roundup of 17 events from Nov 28 to Dec 31.
